## Overview

LRP312 is a **one-knob companion** to [LRP258](../lrp-rli-mech-258/): the same rows,
outcome, own-baseline term, adjustment set, subject random intercept, priors, and — as
LRP258 is itself matched to LRP58 — the same reduced six-function HSGP basis, tight
length-scale prior and raised acceptance target. It differs in exactly one thing. Where
LRP258 adjusts for measured ability with `blocks` (WPPSI-III Block Design) alone, this
fit uses the two-subtest composite `objass_c` — Block Design plus Object Assembly.

Where the LRP306–311 panel does this for the linear Tier-1 slopes, this does it for the
family's **headline estimand**: the flexible letter-sound curve of
[LRP58](../lrp-rli-mech-058/), whose interquartile contrast is the quantity the mechanism
family publishes.

## Why it exists

LRP258 is the fit that answers "what does the curve look like once measured ability is
partialled out", and the answer on record is that it barely moves — on the family's
declared interquartile estimand the ability-adjusted curve reads +2.7 items (89% +0.6 to
+4.6) against +2.8 (+0.8 to +4.6) for the unadjusted LRP58. That is a load-bearing
robustness claim for the project's most-cited association, and it rests on a single
subtest. The mechanism findings note makes the same point in the other direction: a
single noisy subtest cannot rule the latent node out, because adjusting for a mismeasured
confounder removes only part of its influence. Over the 54 analysed
children Block Design and Object Assembly correlate at 0.664, so Block Design alone is
roughly a 0.66-reliable measure of what they share while their sum is roughly
0.80-reliable. This fit re-reads the claim at the higher reliability.

A better-measured proxy is still a proxy. Both subtests are perceptual-organisation
tasks, so what they share is a **narrow visuospatial factor** — the domain of relative
strength in the Down syndrome profile — and not the latent general ability `GA` of the
project's causal diagram, which stays unmeasured and structurally unblockable. The curve
remains an **adjusted association**, and no adjustment available here makes it a causal
skill-to-skill effect.

## How to read it

Compare with **LRP258**, not with the unadjusted LRP58, and compare the declared
interquartile contrast rather than the curve by eye. A screening regression over the
fitted rows expects agreement, so agreement is the result that closes the criticism.

Because the exposure enters as a Hilbert-space Gaussian-process term, **check the
convergence gate before reading anything**. LRP258's own history shows this geometry is
the demanding part of the family, and the ability term is not what makes it hard: a
failed gate here is a computation problem, not evidence about ability.

## Model

$$
\eta = \alpha + \alpha_{\text{phase}} + \beta_G G
  + f_{\text{mech}}\!\left(z(\operatorname{logit}_* L_{\text{post}})\right)
  + \gamma_{\text{own}}\operatorname{logit}_*(W_{\text{pre}})
  + \gamma_A z(A) + \gamma_{\text{objass}} z(\text{objass\_c})
  + \sum_c \gamma_c z(c) + u_{\text{child}}.
$$

The only difference from LRP258 is that $\gamma_{\text{blocks}} z(\text{blocks})$ is
replaced by $\gamma_{\text{objass}} z(\text{objass\_c})$. The composite is the raw sum of
the two subtests, derived by
`statistical_models.preprocessing.derive_nonverbal_ability_composite`; the subtests have
near-equal spread in this cohort, so the sum agrees with the average of their
standardised scores to a correlation of 0.99984, and it is standardised here in any case.
